config.prompt: Explain, in a few paragraphs, how a write-ahead log lets a database recover after a crash.

reference.text:
A write-ahead log is a file that contains a record of all changes made to the database. When a change is made to the database, the change is first written to the log, and then the change is written to the database itself. This ensures that the log always contains a record of the most recent changes made to the database, even if the database itself is not up to date.
When a crash occurs, the database can use the log to recover the most recent changes. The database can read the log and apply the changes to the database, effectively undoing any changes that were made before the crash. This ensures that the database is always in a consistent state, even after a crash.
The write-ahead log also helps to prevent data loss in the event of a crash. This ensures that the log always contains a complete and accurate record of all changes made to the database, even if the database itself is corrupted or lost.
When a database crashes, the write-ahead log can be used to recover the database to a consistent state. The log is scanned to determine the last consistent point in the database, and all changes made after that point are discarded. The database is then rebuilt from the log, using the changes that were made before the crash. This ensures that the database is recovered to a consistent state, with all changes that were made before the crash being preserved.
